title: Former Blue Jay, wife charged with fraud linked to Ontario youth baseball program fees: police

image.caption: Michelle Butler, 52, and former professional baseball player Richard Butler, 53, are facing multiple charges after a fraud investigation focusing on the Ontario Devil Rays training program. (Durham Regional Police Services)

blocks.text: Former big leaguer Richard Butler and his wife, Michelle, have been charged after a fraud investigation into the Ontario Devil Rays baseball training program, which allegedly took thousands of dollars for training it never provided, Durham police say.
Former big leaguer Richard Butler and his wife Michelle are facing 3 charges each

A former Major League Baseball player and his wife have been charged after a fraud investigation into an Ontario youth baseball program, which allegedly took thousands of dollars for training it never provided, Durham police say.

Between April 1 and Oct. 31 of last year, approximately $60,000 in registration fees for the 2025-2026 Ontario Devil Rays training program was deposited into a bank account associated with the program, police said in a news release Tuesday. But funds were later transferred to other accounts associated with the accused — Michelle Butler, 52, and former big leaguer Richard Butler, 53, both of Frankfurt, Ont.
The registration fees were allegedly not used for the program, and the services agreed upon were not provided, police said.

Families who paid the registration received an email on Oct. 19, 2025, saying the business had been dissolved due to financial hardship and claiming bankruptcy, police said. But investigators later determined the lawyer’s name on the email “had allegedly been used without his knowledge or permission, and no bankruptcy or insolvency proceedings were initiated,” the release said.
Rich Butler spent parts of three seasons in the big leagues, including a long sting with the Tampa Bay Devil Rays during the team's first season in the MLB. (Getty Images, David Seelig/Allsport)
Richard and Michelle Butler have now been charged with one count each of fraud over $5,000, possession of property obtained by crime over $5,000 and uttering a forged document.

Richard Butler played parts of three seasons in the big leagues, including seven games for the Toronto Blue Jays in 1997 and 79 games for the Tampa Bay Rays between 1998 and 1999, according to the Major League Baseball website.
Police say they are concerned there may be further victims. Anyone with information is asked to contact Durham police.
